title: The seven aspects of project performance
blurb: List and explain the seven aspects of performance that every PRINCE2 7 project must manage, including sustainability.
question: A project board sets a limit on the carbon emissions its new depot may produce during construction. Which aspect of project performance is the board managing?

teach.h: Seven things to keep under control
teach.body: PRINCE2 7 names seven aspects of project performance to be managed: benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk. They are the project's performance targets, and they are also the seven areas against which tolerances can be set. Plain English: these are the seven dials the project board and project manager watch to know whether the project is on track.

teach.h: Busy Cooks Taste Quality Soups, Spice Rice
teach.caption: Two S words: scope, then sustainability (the new one).

head: Aspect
The question
Tolerance example
rows: Who is it for; what justifies it?
When does it start, deliver, end?
teach.caption: Figures are illustrations; real tolerances are set by the business layer and project board.

teach.body: Benefits: the team must understand the purpose and what must be achieved to justify the investment. Costs: the project has to be affordable, without overspend or underspend. Time: start, key deliveries and finish. Quality: on time and on budget is little comfort if the result does not work. Scope: what the plan's products are. Sustainability: every project affects its environment, so targets are needed. Risk: limits on the plan's aggregated risks.

teach.caption: Any revision material listing six aspects is out of date.

teach.body: Halden Rail is adding step-free access to a station. Project manager Ama Mensah agrees targets for all seven aspects: benefits (more passengers using the station), costs (£3.2m), time (open before the summer timetable), quality (lifts meet the accessibility specification), scope (two lifts and a footbridge), sustainability (a cap on construction emissions) and risk (a limit on the plan's total risk exposure). Tolerances around each tell her when to escalate.

teach.h: Which aspect is this target about?

teach.text: Scope is about the plan's PRODUCTS (what will be delivered); scope tolerance is permitted variation in those products. Variation in forecast benefits is BENEFITS tolerance. And any list of six aspects without sustainability is the old 6th edition.

items: Seven aspects: benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk (1.4).
They are the project's performance targets and the seven areas for tolerances.
Sustainability is new in PRINCE2 7: projects affect their environment, so teams need sustainability targets for the work and the products.
Scope = what the plan's products are; quality = products fit for purpose; risk = limits on aggregated risk.

summary: You can now list the seven aspects of project performance and explain what each one covers. You can also recognize which aspect a target or tolerance belongs to, and spot out-of-date lists that miss sustainability.

A.q: Which is one of the seven aspects of project performance in PRINCE2 7?
A.why: The seven aspects are benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk (1.4).

whyNot.0: Communication is handled through the people element and communication management approach, not as a performance aspect.
whyNot.1: Governance is provided by the business layer and project board, not listed as a performance aspect.
whyNot.3: Stakeholders are engaged through the people element; they are not one of the seven aspects.

A.q: Which aspect of performance asks when the project will start, when key products will be delivered and when it will finish?
A.why: Time covers when the project starts, when key products are delivered and when it finishes.

whyNot.0: Scope covers what the project will deliver, not when.
whyNot.2: Costs cover affordability and spend against budget.
whyNot.3: Benefits cover who the project is for and what must be achieved to justify it.

A.q: Which aspect of project performance was added in PRINCE2 7?
A.why: PRINCE2 7 added sustainability, taking the aspects (and tolerance areas) from six to seven.

whyNot.0: Risk was already an aspect and tolerance area in the 6th edition.
whyNot.1: Quality was already an aspect in the 6th edition.
whyNot.2: Benefits was already an aspect in the 6th edition.

B.q: A project board states that the combined exposure from all the threats in the plan must stay within an agreed limit. Which aspect of performance is this?
B.why: The risk aspect concerns limits on the plan's aggregated risks.

whyNot.1: Costs concern affordability and spend; this target is about combined risk exposure.
whyNot.2: Quality concerns products being fit for purpose.
whyNot.3: Benefits concern what must be achieved to justify the investment.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Finishing on time and within budget is little consolation if the products do not work, so the [?] aspect requires that what is delivered is fit for purpose.
B.why: The quality aspect: what the project delivers must be fit for purpose, as specified and working.

whyNot.0: Scope is about what products will be delivered, not whether they are fit for purpose.
whyNot.1: Benefits concern the measurable improvements that justify the project.
whyNot.3: Sustainability concerns the project's environmental, social and economic targets.

B.q:
Which two statements about the aspects of project performance are correct?
1. PRINCE2 7 names seven aspects of performance.
2. Sustainability replaced risk as an aspect in PRINCE2 7.
3. Tolerances can be set against the aspects of performance.
4. Scope describes the benefits the project should realize.
B.why: There are seven aspects (statement 1), and they are also the areas against which tolerances are set (statement 3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: sustainability was added; risk remains an aspect.
whyNot.1: Statements 2 and 4 are false: risk remains an aspect, and scope describes the products, not the benefits.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: scope is about the plan's products; benefits are a separate aspect.

C.q: A project board wants construction emissions on a new station to stay within an agreed limit, and the new lifts to meet their accessibility specification. Which two aspects of performance is it managing?
C.why: An emissions limit is a sustainability target; lifts meeting their specification is about quality (fit for purpose, as specified).

whyNot.0: Neither target is about the plan's aggregated risk, and meeting a specification is quality rather than scope.
whyNot.2: The emissions limit is sustainability, but meeting a specification is quality; scope is which products are delivered.
whyNot.3: Meeting the specification is quality, but an emissions limit is sustainability, not benefits.

C.q: Which aspect concerns what the project will deliver, and what does its tolerance allow?
options: Scope; a permitted variation in the plan's products
Benefits; a permitted variation in the plan's products
Scope; a permitted variation in forecast benefits
Quality; a permitted variation in the stage's costs
C.why: Scope is what the plan's products are, and scope tolerance is the permissible variation in those products.

whyNot.1: Benefits concern the value that justifies the project, not what products are delivered.
whyNot.2: Variation in forecast benefits is benefits tolerance, not scope tolerance.
whyNot.3: Quality concerns fitness for purpose, and cost variation is cost tolerance.

C.q: According to PRINCE2 7, who needs to know the sustainability performance targets, and for what?
options: The business layer, for the organization's yearly ESG report
The users, for the products once the project has closed
The project management team, for both the work and its products
The supplier, for the contract terms covering its own staff
C.why: Every project affects its environment, so project management teams need the sustainability performance targets for the project work and for the products required.

whyNot.0: The business sets ESG commitments, but the aspect is about the project team knowing targets for the project's work and products.
whyNot.1: The targets apply during the project to the work and the products, and are managed by the project management team.
whyNot.3: Sustainability targets are not limited to contract terms; they cover the project work and its products.

reteach.title: Think of a car's dashboard
reteach.question: A driver watches several dials at once: speed, fuel, temperature and more. How are the seven aspects like a project dashboard?

blocks.body: Each aspect is a dial with a target and a safe range. Costs is the fuel gauge, time is the clock, scope is the route you agreed to take, quality is whether the car still runs properly, risk is how close you drive to the edge, benefits is the reason for the trip, and sustainability is the emissions you are allowed. If any needle is forecast to leave its safe range, the driver tells the person who set the range.

blocks.text: Seven dials, not six: sustainability is the one older material leaves out.

explain.body: Benefits: who the project is for and what must be achieved to justify the investment. Costs: the project must be affordable, and overspend or underspend against the budget must be managed.

test.q: Which aspect asks who the project is for and what must be achieved to justify its investment?
test.why: The benefits aspect asks who the project is for and what must be achieved to justify the investment.

whyNot.0: Costs concern affordability, not who the project is for.
whyNot.1: Scope concerns what the project will deliver.
whyNot.2: Risk concerns limits on the plan's aggregated risks.

explain.body: Time: when the project starts, when key products are delivered and when it finishes. Scope: what the project will deliver, meaning the products in the plan.

test.q: Which aspect of performance concerns what the project will deliver?
test.why: Scope is what the project will deliver: the products in the plan.

whyNot.0: Time concerns when things happen, not what is delivered.
whyNot.1: Quality concerns whether the products are fit for purpose.
whyNot.3: Benefits concern the improvements that justify the project.

explain.body: Quality: what is delivered must be fit for purpose, as specified and working. Risk: the project sets limits on the plan's aggregated risks, so exposure stays acceptable.

test.q: Which aspect of performance requires that the project's products are fit for purpose?
test.why: The quality aspect requires that what the project delivers is fit for purpose: as specified and working.

whyNot.1: Risk concerns limits on aggregated risks, not product fitness.
whyNot.2: Scope concerns which products are delivered, not whether they are fit for purpose.
whyNot.3: Sustainability concerns environmental and wider targets for the work and products.

explain.body: New in PRINCE2 7. Every project affects its environment, so the project management team needs sustainability performance targets for the project work and the products. Sustainability tolerance sets limits on the agreed sustainability metrics.

test.q: Why does PRINCE2 7 include sustainability as an aspect of performance?
options: Every project affects its environment, so targets are needed
It replaces risk, which is now handled by the business layer
It is required for projects that are part of a programme
It measures how long the products last after handover
test.why: All projects have an impact on their environment, so teams need sustainability performance targets for the project work and products.

whyNot.1: Risk remains one of the seven aspects; sustainability was added, not swapped in.
whyNot.2: Sustainability applies to every project, standalone or within a programme.
whyNot.3: Product lifespan is not how the aspect is defined; it concerns sustainability targets for the work and products.
